newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH PM SAYS GOVT AGREES CABINET CHANGES.
newsitem.headline: CZECH PM SAYS GOVT AGREES CABINET CHANGES.

text.p: Czech Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus said on Wednesday his three-party ruling coalition had reached agreement on an economic recovery and stabilisation programme and on personnel changes to the cabinet.
After a more than six-hour meeting, Klaus began reading a long statement setting out the changes.
Klaus told a news conference that former Education Minister Ivan Pilip would take over as Finance Minister and Czech ambassador to Britain Karel Kuhnl would be the new Industry and Trade Minister.
The government agreed last week to make changes to the cabinet in the wake of a sharp fall in its popularity sparked by an economic downturn.
The changes have been eagerly awaited by the foreign exchange markets since the central bank gave in to speculative selling of the crown and, from Tuesday, allowed the currency to float.
The crown came under severe selling pressure from investors didsmayed at the worseing economic situation and political uncertainty.
